title: Living Without All the Answers
overview: The writer weighs how to live wisely under powerful rulers and in a world where justice often seems missing, and admits that no one can fully understand what God is doing.

parts.label: Wisdom before the king (vv. 1-6)
parts.note: Wisdom shows on a person's face and softens a hard look, and part of wisdom is knowing how to act before a ruler whose word is final. Keep the loyalty you swore with God as witness, do not rush out of his presence or stick with a wrong cause, and wait for the right time and way to act; most read 'king' as an earthly ruler, though some older interpreters took it to mean God.

parts.label: No one controls death (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: No one knows what is coming, and no one can hold on to the breath of life on the day of death. Just as soldiers could not simply walk away from a war, doing wrong will not set anyone free from what is coming.

parts.label: The wicked honored (vv. 9-10)
parts.note: The writer sees one person ruling over another 'to his hurt', and the Hebrew could mean harm to the people ruled or to the ruler himself. He also sees wicked people buried with honor after coming and going from the holy place and being praised in the city, though the Hebrew of verse 10 is unclear, so translations differ on who is praised and who is forgotten.

parts.label: Justice delayed (vv. 11-13)
parts.note: When punishment is slow, people grow bold to do wrong, and a wicked person may live long. Even so, the writer says it will go better for those who stand in awe of God, though scholars debate whether this is his firm belief or a traditional view he is holding up against what he sees.

parts.label: When life seems upside down (vv. 14-15)
parts.note: Sometimes good people get what the wicked deserve and the wicked get what the good deserve, and he calls this senseless. His response is to recommend enjoying food, drink and gladness as part of the life God gives, alongside daily work.

parts.label: The limits of understanding (vv. 16-17)
parts.note: Even with sleepless effort, no one can work out the full meaning of what God does in the world. Anyone who claims to have figured it out, even the wise, does not truly know.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether this chapter ultimately expresses trust that God's justice will win out, as verses 12 and 13 suggest, or an honest doubt about life's fairness that the writer leaves largely unresolved.
think: When you see that life does not reward people as they seem to deserve, what do you think is a reasonable way to respond?
